name: Fendi
why: Leather goods and fur from a Roman workshop that grew into a full fashion house; owned by LVMH.
origin: Founded in Rome in 1925 by Adele and Edoardo Fendi.

onething.n: SSENSE designer page — MP search deep-links are dead

notes.ital: Roman before it is fashion — furriers on Via del Plebiscito from 1925, five sisters, and a double-F that Lagerfeld drew in a few seconds. The city is legible in the maximalism.
notes.status: The FF worn as ornament rather than concealed. Roman maximalism, and the status is in the visibility.

notes.craft: Fendi's men's ready-to-wear PDPs state 'Made in Italy' and composition, and name no maker or mill. The US content sitemap lists client-service, authentication and campaign pages but nothing on factories or how things are made. On what could be shown at a primary source this is country-of-make only = 2. [held at the current score: the audit’s evidence was thin; needs a second read]

craft_evidence.owned_d: No owned factory or workshop seen at a primary source in this run. fendi.com content sitemap lists no factory/craftsmanship pages; men's RTW listing has no craftsmanship links; guessed fendi.com and lvmh.com factory/maison URLs returned 404. Context only (Wikipedia, does not score): 'around 400 in specialist leather and fur ateliers in Italy' as of 2018, no place named. Fendi is an LVMH maison; any owned making would be Fendi's within LVMH, likely leather goods/fur rather than RTW, but this is unverified.
craft_evidence.countries: Italy 3/4 (sample of 4 men's RTW PDPs: sweater, bomber, t-shirt = Made in Italy; denim shirt page showed no origin or composition, possibly in a collapsed tab the fetch couldn't see). Shoes and bags not sampled.
